To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Ontology is the philosophical discipline that studies the nature of being, becoming, existence or reality, as well as the basic categories of being and their relations; (2) In information science, ontologies are used to describe a reality and to validate both conceptual models and schemas; (3) Ontologies for information systems are used in the development and maintenance of the information system.

Ontology (with capital O) is the basic description in Philosophy of the reality in the world, and that ontologies are engineering artifacts, constituted by a vocabulary used for the description of the reality in a specific domain.
ontologies have a double role in information science research and that these two roles are not the same.

a clarification of the meaning of Ontology and of the different uses of ontologies in Information Science.
the use of Ontologies (with a capital 'O') in the development and evaluation of conceptual models and conceptual schema.
a better understanding of the concept of ontologies in Information Science.

Ontology and ontological analysis are useful in the design of information systems.

the term Ontology is a philosophical concept that is being misused in information science.
